q: How much coal and CO2 does a 250 kW biomass gasifier save in a tea dryer?
title: Tea dryer: 250 kW biomass gasifier on coal
short: BEE's Jorhat report counts 258 t of coal saved a year, about 453 t of fossil CO2, burning 342 t of garden wood. Only 173 t of that coal is the gasifier; 85 t comes from a better burner on the coal heater, which keeps running. Cost Rs 17.18 lakh, payback 3.70 years at 2010 prices.
audience: Tea factories in Jorhat and upper Assam drying on coal-fired air heaters with woody biomass from their own gardens

ul: 225 kg of made tea an hour at 950 kcal per kg; the coal heater runs at 19.81% efficiency and burns 240 kg an hour.
12 hours a day, 300 days: 3,600 hours and 863.2 t of coal a year at 4,500 kcal/kg and Rs 4.50 a kg.
A better burner lifts efficiency to 21.97%: 216 kg an hour, 84.9 t a year less.
The gasifier makes 250 kW of heat, 215,000 kcal an hour, as producer gas at about 1,000 kcal/m3, replacing 48 kg of coal an hour: 172.8 t a year.
Wood from the tea gardens at 95 kg an hour, 342 t a year at Rs 1.75 a kg.

p: After both changes the factory still burns about 605 t of coal a year, 70% of what it burned before. A 250 kW gasifier supplies only part of the dryer's heat. Size it against your full heat demand if you want coal gone.

257.67 t of coal x 1.76 = 453 t of fossil CO2 avoided. CO2 from the wood is biogenic and reported separately. The report's 468.12 t used a higher coal factor. Assam coal often carries more carbon than India's average, so use your supplier's calorific value or a lab analysis if you have one.

sections.h: One figure to get in writing
p: The specification table rates the gasifier at 250 kg of wood an hour; the costing uses 95 kg. At 250 kg an hour, wood would cost Rs 15.75 lakh a year against Rs 11.59 lakh of coal saved, and the project would lose money. Ask the supplier to guarantee kg of wood per hour at 250 kW.

example.title: One season of 3,600 hours
lines: Burner: 863.2 t x (1 minus 19.81 / 21.97) = 84.9 t coal
Gasifier: 48 kg an hour x 3,600 = 172.8 t coal
Total: 257.7 t coal x 1.76 = 453.5 t CO2 avoided
Coal still burned: 863.2 minus 257.7 = 605.5 t, about 1,066 t CO2
example.note: Coal at our Indian coal factor, an estimate. The report gives no figure for the gasifier's blower power.
